smt-2021-combo-01.title: Condition on the outcome
smt-2021-combo-01.body:
An ordinary roll has expected value $\frac{1+2+\cdots+6}{6}=3.5$. The roll exceeds $3.5$ exactly when it is $4$, $5$ or $6$, each equally likely. The conditional expectation is $\frac{4+5+6}{3}=5$.

**Answer: 5**

smt-2021-combo-02.title: Inclusion-exclusion
smt-2021-combo-02.body:
Let $A,B,C$ be the events that positions $1$-$3$, $2$-$4$, $3$-$5$ respectively are in increasing order. $|A|=|B|=|C|=\binom53\cdot2!=20$ (choose which three students go there, order is forced, arrange the other two). $|A\cap B|=|B\cap C|=\binom54=5$ (four consecutive increasing), $|A\cap C|=|A\cap B\cap C|=1$ (all five increasing). So $|A\cup B\cup C|=60-(5+5+1)+1=50$.

Bad-free arrangements: $120-50=70$, probability $\frac{70}{120}=\frac7{12}$, so $m+n=19$.

**Answer: 19**

smt-2021-combo-03.title: Alternating changes
smt-2021-combo-03.body:
Reading along the sequence, each "$01$" or "$10$" is a change of value, and the changes alternate between $01$ and $10$. So the counts of $01$ and $10$ differ by at most $1$, and they are equal exactly when the number of changes is even, i.e. when the first and last entries are equal. That happens with probability $\frac12$. So $m+n=1+2=3$.

**Answer: 3**

smt-2021-combo-04.title: Fix one corner
smt-2021-combo-04.body:
Each unit cube has three painted faces meeting at a corner, so it must sit at a corner of the big cube with its painted corner outward, which can be done in $3$ orientations. Use the rotations of the whole cube to place one particular unit cube in a fixed corner with a fixed orientation (rotations of the whole cube act freely on such placements). The other $7$ unit cubes can then go in the remaining $7$ positions in $7!$ ways, each in $3$ orientations: $N=7!\cdot3^7$. So $a=7$, $b=7$, $p=3$ and $a+b+p=17$.

**Answer: 17**

smt-2021-combo-04.title: Count all, divide by rotations
smt-2021-combo-04.body:
Without identifying rotations there are $8!\cdot3^8$ arrangements, and the $24$ rotations of the cube give $24$ equivalent copies of each. $N=\frac{8!\cdot3^8}{24}=7!\cdot3^7$, hence $17$.

**Answer: 17**

smt-2021-combo-05.title: Winning chance of the first roller
smt-2021-combo-05.body:
In a round the first roller wins with probability $\frac{1/6}{1-(5/6)^2}=\frac6{11}$, so the second roller wins with probability $\frac5{11}$.

Let $x_r$ be the probability that Alice rolls first in round $r$. Then $x_1=1$ and, since the loser of round $r$ rolls first in round $r+1$, $x_{r+1}=\frac5{11}x_r+\frac6{11}(1-x_r)$ (Alice loses with probability $\frac5{11}$ if she rolled first and $\frac6{11}$ if she rolled second). So $x_2=\frac5{11}$, $x_3=\frac{5}{11}\cdot\frac5{11}+\frac{6}{11}\cdot\frac{6}{11}=\frac{61}{121}$, $x_4=\frac{61}{121}\cdot\frac5{11}+\frac{60}{121}\cdot\frac6{11}=\frac{665}{1331}$. $665$ and $1331=11^3$ are coprime, so $A+B=665+1331=1996$.

**Answer: 1996**

smt-2021-combo-06.title: Reflection
smt-2021-combo-06.body:
The frog's path must never reach the line $y=x-7$. Total paths: $\binom{20}{7}$. A path touching $y=x-7$: reflect the part after the first touch in that line; the endpoint $(13,7)$ goes to $(14,6)$, giving a bijection with all paths to $(14,6)$, of which there are $\binom{20}{6}$.

$N=\binom{20}7-\binom{20}6=77520-38760=38760$, and $\frac{N}{120}=323$.

**Answer: 323**

smt-2021-combo-07.title: Probability of visiting each sum
smt-2021-combo-07.body:
Let $N=2020$ and $u_j$ the probability that the running sum is exactly $j$ at some time. Then $u_0=1$ and $u_j=\frac1N\sum_{i<j}u_i$, so $u_j=\frac1N\left(1+\frac1N\right)^{j-1}$ for $1\le j\le N$.

She stops at $s$ ($N\le s\le 2N-1$) iff the last sum below $N$ was some $j\ge s-N$ and she then rolled $s-j$: $P(s)=\frac1N\sum_{j=s-N}^{N-1}u_j$. This shrinks as $s$ grows, so $X=N=2020$ and $Y=2N-1=4039$.

$P(X)=\frac1N\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}u_j=u_N=\frac1N\left(1+\frac1N\right)^{N-1}$ and $P(Y)=\frac{u_{N-1}}{N}=\frac1{N^2}\left(1+\frac1N\right)^{N-2}$.

Therefore $\frac{P(Y)}{P(X)}=\frac{1/N}{1+1/N}=\frac1{N+1}=\frac1{2021}$.

**Answer: $\frac1{2021}$**

smt-2021-combo-08.title: Small boards fail, $n=5$ works
smt-2021-combo-08.body:
For $n\le 4$ Xavier can always prevent a line from having $3$ more O's than X's (a computer search of the full game tree for $n=3,4$ confirms this; $n\le2$ is trivial since a line has at most $2$ cells).

For $n=5$: if after Oliver's move some line has $2$ more O's than X's, Xavier is forced to reply in that line, so Oliver can steer Xavier's moves with such threats and build a double threat. A complete search of the game tree shows that Oliver can force a line with $3$ more O's than X's within $6$ turns, so he wins on a $5\times5$ board.

So the minimum is $n=5$.

**Answer: 5**

smt-2021-combo-09.title: Recursion
smt-2021-combo-09.body:
Let $T(n)$ be the number of valid schedules of $n$ days. Tracking the last two days (break+instrument, instrument+break, two different instruments, same instrument twice) gives the recurrence $T(n)=T(n-1)+T(n-2)+T(n-3)$ for $n\ge5$, with $T(2)=8$, $T(3)=12$, $T(4)=24$. Then $T(5)=44$, $T(6)=80$, $T(7)=148$, $T(8)=272$.

**Answer: 272**

smt-2021-combo-09.title: Computer check
smt-2021-combo-09.body:
Enumerating all $3^8$ sequences of V/P/B (violin, piano, break) and discarding those in which V or P is absent for $3$ consecutive days gives $272$.

**Answer: 272**

smt-2021-combo-10.title: Burnside's lemma
smt-2021-combo-10.body:
Count subsets of $\mathbb Z_{12}$ up to cyclic shift, including the empty set and singletons, then remove them. A shift by $k$ fixes a subset exactly when the subset is a union of cosets of the subgroup generated by $k$, giving $2^{\gcd(k,12)}$ fixed subsets. Summing over $k=0,\dots,11$: $2^{12}+4\cdot2^1+2\cdot2^2+2\cdot2^3+2\cdot2^4+2^6=4096+8+8+16+32+64=4224$. Divide by $12$: $352$ orbits.

The empty set and the $12$ singletons form $2$ orbits (empty; one-note), so the number of chords is $352-2=350$.

**Answer: 350**

smt-2021-combo-10.title: Computer check
smt-2021-combo-10.body:
Enumerating all $4096$ subsets, keeping those of size at least $2$, and identifying subsets related by rotation gives $350$ classes.

**Answer: 350**
